summary.text: 回 is an indivisible picture-like graph associated with turning or circular motion. Its exact early referent and meaning are uncertain; today it commonly means “return” or “turn around,” and it also counts occurrences.

formation.text: Pictographic analysis is the best-supported account in this dossier: the graph is interpreted as a spiral or revolving shape. One reference specifies water turning in a circle, but the physical referent and exact original meaning are not established. A competing analysis argues that 囘 and 回 were originally separate graphs and words, with 回 meaning “around”; this remains unresolved. The character should be treated as a whole image rather than divided into independently established semantic or phonetic parts.

components.text: 回 is analyzed here as one whole pictorial graph associated with a spiral or circular motion. The descriptions of outer 囗 and an inner revolving form belong to a historical account, not a securely established division into components.

history.text: Historical accounts describe circular or revolving forms, and a reference labels displayed forms as oracle-bone, bronze, seal, and clerical script. Those labels do not provide a verified specimen sequence here; no glyph image was independently inspected, so they should not be read as demonstrated evolutionary steps.

The traditional account parses the graph as outer 囗 with an inner shape resembling rotation. A modern scholarly alternative treats 囘 and 回 as originally distinct graphs and words, proposing that 回 was made for “around” and followed the shape of 圍. The available evidence does not settle their relationship.

回 is reported as a sound-and-meaning component in 迴. The graphs have matching Mandarin huí and corresponding historical readings in the cited reconstruction systems; this later compound role does not establish a phonetic element in 回’s own origin.

uncertainties.text: The dossier supports a spiral or circular-motion interpretation, but does not establish the depicted object or exact earliest meaning. The competing account distinguishing 囘 and 回 is available only in abstract-level evidence and cannot be fully assessed here.

No securely dated contextual occurrence was examined to establish the earliest attested sense or a chronology linking turning, returning, replying, and occurrence-counting uses. Dictionary gloss lists and cited literary examples do not by themselves establish that sequence.
The proposed derivation of the ethnonym 回回 from Uyghur or Old Turkic forms is not independently verified in this dossier; its source word and historical sound match remain unestablished here.
The sound relationship between 回 and 迴 is supported, but the date when 迴 arose or when the two graphs came to be variant or distributionally distinct spellings is not established.

senses.text: Turning or revolving is the earliest meaning proposed by the pictographic and traditional accounts, but no securely dated contextual occurrence establishes it as the earliest attested sense.
“Return” is a current common meaning listed for 回. The dossier does not establish when it developed in relation to the turning sense.
回 is also used for a time or occurrence, including as a counter. The supplied glosses do not date this use or show how it developed.

limitations.text: The available examples and dictionary glosses do not establish the chronology or semantic pathway connecting turn, return, and occurrence-counting uses.

A proposed 回回 ethnonym borrowing is a separate account of a word written with this graph, not evidence that the character’s meaning developed into an ethnonym. The source and sound-based borrowing remain unverified in this dossier.

overview.text: 回 is a whole, picture-like graph associated with turning or circular motion. Its exact early referent is uncertain. Common uses include “return” and counting an occurrence.

components.text: Read the graph as one whole picture associated with circular motion; its outer and inner shapes are not established as separate meaning-bearing parts.
